newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pioneer sees refiner margin pressure.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer sees refiner margin pressure.

text.p: Pioneer International Ltd chief executive John Schubert said on Friday he expected weak petroleum refiner margins for up to the next two years due to the startup of new refineries in Asia recently.
Pioneer jointly owns Australia's largest petroleum retail and refining group, Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd, which trades as Ampol, with Caltex Australia Ltd.
"I think there is going to be an over-supply for some time so I am not expecting refiner margins to be terribly good for the next year or two," Schubert told reporters after Pioneer's annual meeting.
Schubert said the margin pressure was due to over-supply as a result of new refineries starting over the past two years.
"I think fundamentally it (the refiner market) is the worst I have seen in the last four or five years," Schubert said.
He said refiner margins were currently virtually zero.
Historically, refiner margins do not stay at the same level for too long as refiners normally take action to improve the situation, he said.
"It can't last very long, actions are going to be taken," he said. He said the refiner margin in the first quarter for Ampol was lower than any quarter in the 1995/96 year to June 30.
